Also heard Mr. R. J. Baruah, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State of Assam.
The petitioner was arrested on 14.03.2023 and he is behind bar for last 189 days.

This Court under its order dated 08.08.2023, as called for the LCR along with the deposition of Md Asadul Ali @ Hussain vs The State Of Assam on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62588150/

sentences.text: The victim lady has thoroughly been examined by the prosecution and cross-examined by the defence.

From the perusal of the materials on record, she is the star witness for the prosecution and as she has already been examined and cross-examined, this Court is of the view that there is no scope for influence and / or hampering or tampering with the evidence.

Further from the perusal of the testimony of the victim, this Court is of the view that the petitioner should not be kept under further detention inasmuch as he is required to properly defend his case.
Accordingly, the present application is allowed.

It is directed that the petitioner, name above, be released on bail in connection with the case aforementioned, on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned learned Additional Sessions Judge (FTC), Lakhimpur, with the following conditions.
In terms of the above, this bail application stands disposed of.
